reason: The fixed populations, all potential-response formulas, nondegenerate independent assignment, complete arm support laws, numerical effects and covariances render the canonical witnesses correctly. The exported conjunction does not separately assert A4's pointwise observed-support cancellation formula, B1's exact pointwise K(0) and K(1) formulas, or B3's two conditional observed-support arm means of 59/25. Those facts remain true consequences of the definitions; the smaller explicit conclusion set is the restriction being assessed. The counterexamples contradict an unconditional extension only, not the paper's contextual conditional with D >= 0. Exact rational enumeration confirms the finite numerical and distributional assertions; all finite weights and assignment probabilities are positive.

For arbitrary probability spaces the independent Bernoulli product law and observedSupport encode assignment independence and consistency. The only substantive premises are 0 < p < 1 and integrability of exactly the canonical five potential variables. All decomposition, pointwise, weak/strict sign, null, linear, positive-a ratio and finite-channel assertions are present, together with the counterexample to dropping D >= 0. Integrability here supplies almost-everywhere measurability and finite absolute expectations, so the Bochner integrals are not default-zero placeholders. Product arm masses are p and 1-p, both positive. A Dirac probability law on Unit with K(t)=t and S(t,k)=k is a Lean-checked satisfying instance.

Both exact constructions, their positive first stages, exclusion and consistency by construction, bounds, monotone support responses, individual increaser increments, complete observable laws, unequal conditional increaser effects and full-law nonidentification are faithfully rendered. The conjunction does not separately export the universal normalized nonnegative weighted-average assertion of (a3), or the exact five-type increaser probabilities 2/5 and 3/5 in (b3). It retains nonzero probabilities for both conditional means. These omissions are not false claims: all three increaser probabilities (2/3, 2/5, 3/5) were proved from Defs in scratch/Check.lean, and independent rational enumeration confirms all fixed numerical laws. The construction refutes the stated sufficient-assumptions reading of the paper's IV guidance, not any empirical estimate.

The crossed-margin definitions and normalized formula agree with the canonical claim, with no sign premise on response increments. Coverage is restricted to finite latent-type populations with arbitrary nonnegative real weights of total one, whereas the canonical statement and definitions allow general probability laws; the note that a finite population suffices does not remove this difference. Identification and covariance conclusions (i) remain under the outer monotonicity and positive-first-stage premises, instead of being independently exported from (H1)-(H3). General bounded signed telescoping and the downward-crossing implication are present, but arbitrary-nonmonotone signed-crossing value-set membership, the particular T4 down-type R(9)=-1 equality and the separate nonidentification assertion without monotonicity are not separately exported. Conditional increments in the weighted formula are filtered to positive-probability margins; positivity of the first stage guards its normalization. A Lean-checked two-type example with K(0)=8 and K(1)=9 or 10 has J=10 and first stage 3/2, so the hypotheses are jointly satisfiable.

Taking K=q+1 and shifting the labels from 1,...,K to 0,...,q gives exactly the corrected observation/stratum indicator, both stratum-effect cases, the reference-indicator identity, and the regression/stratum-intercept equivalence for arbitrary binary X and real coefficients and disturbances. No estimation or average-treatment-effect claim is added. The q=0 case is the valid K=1 model, and the theorem covers every n rather than relying on n=0. A Lean-checked n=2, q=1 instance occupies both strata and has stratum effects 7 and 0.
